notes.title: Smells like human, tastes like chicken
notes.notes:
[h1]What's up,[/h1]

Dear friends, do you remember the fairy tale of the three pigs hiding from the scurrying wolf? In our tale the roles are somewhat reversed. Why just a little? Because while the piglets have been given the status of persecutors, the wolf will not play the victim. That role has been given to the humans. Now the pigs are the oppressors, because, as the saying goes: where there's meat, there's a party!

In that case, where do you get these humans for slaughter? Where do they hide, how do you hunt them and how do you choose the perfect, juiciest one? Today I'm going to give you some real treats that will put all your doubts to rest. After all, everyone has been dreaming of their own professional butchery since piglethood.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/ce82687406f4f5e116f301d7b54a651d58be7f0d.jpg[/img]

[h2]Little human, little human let me in[/h2]
Every young piglet wonders where the meat comes from. From a young age, they hear legends of bloodthirsty humans lurking in the depths of the surrounding waters. There is some truth to this, as the goons are fished out of the river. However, most of them are not dangerous beasts, but rather silly creatures, and it takes some effort to pull one out. But what's not to be done for juicy legs for dinner, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/b902f87d99a751e069c5535a9d48b31c0870b249.jpg[/img]
[h2]Tasty meat is key[/h2]
It is not at all necessary to eat a captured individual immediately. You can enslave it, stuff it full of antibiotics and hope it reproduces. Before we move on to choosing the right breeder, you need to know which humans are the tastiest. The answer is simple: those that are well cared for and well fed; after all, no one wants to eat just the skin alone (although the skin properly fried is really delicious). Well-bred ones are easier to handle, the meat just falls off the bone on its own! There is just one small problem: space on the farm is limited.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/80f124d29a9f7855a61b43718b084b14ecaf07ae.jpg[/img]
[h2]Build a slaughter empire[/h2]
At this point you should ask yourself if you are able to dedicate your entire pig life to becoming the number one butcher in the area. What type of farming will you choose? Will you opt for the convenience of cage farming and go mass production? Or will you go for the juicy free-range humans? The choice is yours, but remember - quality and splendour count. After all, you want to be better than the hated neighbour who drives the latest BMW to pick up hot dogs from the Welmart.

The life of a butcher is not a bed of roses. Especially the lack of opposable thumbs can be a bit of a handicap. But nothing is impossible for pigs, especially when we are driven by the desire to take revenge on a vicious neighbour. [b]So get to work, humans will not skin themselves![/b]

[h3]Enjoy your meal, oink oink.[/h3]

notes.title: Crowd Psychology
notes.notes:
[h1]Dear Tasty Folks,[/h1]

We discovered one thing that everyone knows about. Don't think it's a cross-promo, I just want to introduce you to the thought process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/c28a367ba8976950def0f76ff956dbf942f1f8b9.png[/img]

We recently released Priest Simulator, and Booze Master is now closest to the premiere. The games were developed in parallel, but there was still some difference in quality between them. Sure, we operate on completely different mechanics, although I assess their attractiveness similarly. The problem was that, up to a point, even the underdeveloped features in Priest Simulator were more fun than the pimped-out mechanics in Booze Master. And this dissonance troubled us for months, until at some point, as planned, we implemented a "big detail". Random NPCs.

Let's be clear, if these blunt AIs didn't come into the game, the Booze Master core wouldn't suffer at all. This is just a gimmick, an aesthetic pinch of powdered sugar, but it takes the game's taste to a whole new level. While most of the role of random NPCs comes down to wandering around the village mindlessly and uttering ridiculous taunts, the illusion is persuasive enough to make us believe that we are producing alcohol for living people. The 3D village got the third dimension.

With this knowledge we approach Human Farm. Expect a living town. Not only pigs, cows, dogs and snakes. It will be the greatest fur celebration in the history of video games. Keep hating me if we don't get it.

notes.title: Why is it hard?
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/cc6c2ff6aea88fc1335855067781bbf720795618.jpg[/img]

Hey Fuzz, you awake?

You wonder why it's taking so long to finish the development of Human Farm. The short answer is: because it's hard. Here goes the long one:

It's not a sadist simulator. If you're expecting to play as a butcher and having fun while making bloodbath out of innocent creatures, you're in the wrong place. I assume most of us wouldn't be able to endure hours of such literal bestiality. We believe torturing animals is bad, and not fun at all.

It's hard to make a decent, full-fledged game with a rich plot and voice actors, and gameplay-wise force players to execute terrible behaviours. It's not a movie, you can't just watch. You, the player, are responsible for the course of events. I'm sure it would be easier if we changed the graphics and the story to be more abstract and ribald, but we took on the challenge of making a relatively realistic presentation.

We don't want to deliver cheap thrills, the game is supposed to deliver a dark, poignant experience. We've all agreed we want to have to tell a story about a bloody human farm. The trick is to have a good balance between a gloomy theme and the joy of playing. We do not want to diminish the seriousness of the topic by reducing game to an interactive joke.

It's not easy to make a game about you being bad.

notes.title: Fresh Meat
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/5973f82a1c79bdf3fcc6ff0df58d9bb6290edd35.png[/img]

Yo.

Recently, we have beaten two games whose subject matter is quite similar to ours. Both are about running a pathological restaurant, but it is interesting that they differ in terms of their approach to gameplay.

Ravenous Devils has a mobile game feeling. It's an almost self-fulfilling mechanism that only requires our lazy clicking. Simply speaking, the game is a cookie clicker in the aesthetics of This War of Mine. We are actually relying on the same loop all the time and progression is increasing the amount of what we got in the beginning. It is like ambient / trance music. Beauty lies in the comfort of a safe routine. Relaxing.

Happy's Humble Burger Farm is an economic and arcade game. I don't want to spoil it, but I'll do it anyway: the creators make fun of the loop that they promised at the beginning of the game. It would seem that we are getting an extremely fucked up experiment, as if the production of the game about running restaurant was entrusted to a mad scientist who all his life dreamed of making a boomer shooter. But the truth is, the man behind has a good head on his shoulders. HHBF is carefully thought out and made, all the seemingly dingy elements combine into a perfectly working mechanism that forces you to demonstrate your time management and keyboard skills. Demanding.

And now we find ourselves trying to get both of these things in Human Farm. But maybe unnecessarily, maybe it is not possible at all. What do you expect?

I don't want to bore you with stories like we've tried so hard to deliver demos to the Steam festival. Everyone already knows the standard developer lament. The lament of a person who made every effort to deliver on time, but with heartache she/he had to make a difficult decision to postpone the premiere. But what else can I say? We're in this fucked up situation too.

We did three demos. Two working, one defective.

The latter is Mercyful Flames. Despite the fact that almost all the plans related to the development of the game have been completed, the final version is not satisfactory for us. Simply put, it sucks. We will only release versions of the games that we do not consider a waste of your time. Mercyful Flames still has annoying bugs, performance problems, lighting problems, translation problems, UX problems, sometimes very poor sound and a lot of other shortcomings. Of course, all of this will be eliminated. When? We will not provide any dates. The current festival was a deadline. The lesson we have for the future is that we do not operate on deadlines. We make the game until we can present it with a clear conscience.

notes.title: The Demon Barbers
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/0422ef5e75c16d90d6b8932f268f82d8dc865582.jpg[/img]

I'll try to be more straightforward today. Don't want to waste your time with the wall of text. It's enough for me that I'll be wasting your time with this game.

Last time we stopped on slaughterhouse and the image above. What happens when people are brought to the slaughterhouse? Let's simplify it even more. Imagine you've got:

a) 3 workers,
b) 1 workplace with 1 slot (hook+knife),
c) 1 workplace with 2 slots (bath),
d) 2 people.

Of course, you can do everything on your own, or occupy one of the worplaces, etc. But let's assume you let your workers do their job on their own. What's happening?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/c1cbc39bc68dd30cdebb41ac29e487552a65fbac.png[/img]

We've got demand for such a amount of meat that it requires to kill two people. Those people are transported to the sluaghterhouse. And here comes the algorithm: the oldest one is set to the first workplace, where he is going to be killed by the best of workers. The other two workers have nothing to do, because the first worplace has only one slot. But when the person is killed...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/18940a3f3344c76853b44791b61ec220836c0064.png[/img]

The body is moved to the second worplace. There are two slots, so the two best workers are going to take its hair off. The worker number one is leaving the first workplace and moving to the second one. The second best worker is coming to help him. The third worker can take care of the younger person.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/de2636f0d21218b98142735a24d3358c55475d47.png[/img]

And so on and so forth. Such a system ensures that there will never be the trouble of having two people in one tub, removing rotting corpses, skinning a living person or looking at ten workers cutting one throat.

Hope this makes some sense ːlunar2019deadpanpigː.

PS I swear I won't be drawing anymore. Forgive me for the last time.

notes.title: Slaves Shall Serve
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/b375f3235fcbcf524e03e834303fdd8632a26b1a.jpg[/img]

Just a clickbait title. There are no slaves in Human Farm. Only good workers that are being paid poorly.

At first it wasn't supposed to be that way. We wanted to avoid hardcore coding work, hoping it would be enough to create brainless puppets that would be a background for the main character. The dummies would make you feel like a boss, but you would still have to do everything yourself. What could have gone wrong?

Many things. Above all, we're not creative enough to come up with a mechanics of running a factory without actually managing it. I don't know if anyone has done it before. Such avoidance of tycoonization led us into borrowing from RPGs, point and clicks and arcade games. Unfortunately, we can't focus on the rich storyline, because it's not Hollywood. The same without arcade, as we don't want to make a "funny" pseudo-simulator out of Human Farm. Simply put, we cannot avoid designing thinking employees. I mean middle-minded, but smart enough to trick you. 

Let me introduce you to a super complicated algorithm behind those pig imbeciles. Here is a brief description of the...

[h1]Internal Demand Flow[/h1]

When we reach the status that will allow us to delegate work to others, our main work tool will be a shop computer. The computer helps us to submit a demand for a given product. The most important informations needed to start the production process are the type of goods and the desired number. Let's say we want to order 6 hot dogs and three burgers. The order in the list is very important as all production prioritizes tasks based mainly on this list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/81949ee20fe7cd8f4df6ab5b2f73a1dac55fd6e9.jpg[/img]

The store sends the information to the packing department, the packing department, if it has the right amount of meat (let's leave the matter of packing materials today), starts working. If not, it sends a request to the processing room... and so on and so on until we get to the farm.

A special case is the order sent from the slaughterhouse to the farm, because the slaughterhouse calculates how many individuals need to be slaughtered to develop 6 hot dogs. As you know, six male individuals are required for this process, so if there is one sausage in the cold room, five individuals will arrive from the farm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/de856b16cdb6e7ba14e2a8c8df6c46f5801fbf85.jpg[/img]

I mean, people don't come to the slaughter on their own. They are delivered by a dedicated employee. It just so happens that for the comfort of management (and, of course, the design of this sick game), employees are assigned to specific departments. The "errand boy" is a unique pig. It runs around the factory like a locomotive, passing on all orders and monitoring the demand of each department.

Take, for example, a slaughterhouse...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/0422ef5e75c16d90d6b8932f268f82d8dc865582.jpg[/img]

Or maybe not today. Because this post is getting terribly long. I will describe the work of the slaughterhouse in the next devlog, and call this one [i]Internal Demand Flow[/i].

notes.title: Dog Day Night
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/ba861edc386b9ffb5114b78a6784e221cbb96932.png[/img]

I don't know who comes up with those ideas, but there is a random special day every day. Puddings, doubles, left-handers and condoms have their holidays. On the one hand, good to have an excuse to make a 360 day binge. On the other, you would probably prefer us to get back to work. For example, we should transfer a gentleman from an image to a 3D. But it just so happens that today (or actually it was before midnight), it was dog's day in Poland. [quote="Rob Quinn]You won't see Wilbur joining a Call of Duty session any time soon, but researchers have confirmed that pigs are capable of playing video games. In a study published in the journal Frontiers of Psychology, animal behavior specialist Candace Croney and chimpanzee cognition expert Sarah Boysen says four pigs were trained to manipulate a joystick with their snouts before they were taught to play a simple video game that involved steering a cursor into walls. The researchers say the pigs showed remarkable progress in learning to play the game, which had been designed for chimpanzees, CNET reports. They say food treats helped encouraged the porcine gamers, but they also responded very well to verbal encouragement.

The researchers say it was "no small feat" for the pigs to grasp that the joystick they were moving was having an effect on what was happening on the screen. They say it is "indicative of their behavioral and cognitive flexibility." They say the pigs weren't as good at the game as the chimps it was designed for—partly because their "ability to manipulate objects is significantly less dexterous and flexible." The researchers say touch-screen games might be a better option for further research, which could include examining whether it's possible to directly communicate with the animals through a computer interface. "I don't think this will come as a surprise to anyone that works with pigs," farmer Kate Daniels tells the BBC. "They're not playing Minecraft—but that they can manipulate a situation to get a reward is no surprise at all." (Read more pigs stories.)[/quote]

Today we announce a unique challenge to commemorate the [b]84th anniversary of George Orwell's birth[/b].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/50144a5c1cd2ae07293f4aef4cbde770f232e8b8.gif[/img]

[h3][b]ABOUT THE CHALLENGE [/b][/h3]

As many have noticed, the game is very controversial, but "Human Farm" is not just about entertainment. You'll find in the game a lot of elements of Orwell's work, books, and great films.

Here we want to focus on the movies. Elements of each of the films will be included in the final version of the game. Knowing all the titles from the selected films, the player should have enough info to guess the main purpose and message of the game.

[h3][b]PURPOSE[/b][/h3]

We want to make players find out what Human Farm is all about by themselves. The game is for gamers. We don't want to spoil it for them the best things. On the other hand, we want to reward those who are clever enough and find out the purpose of the game before the release and give pleasure in participating in a new form of devlogs. 
[u]Don't be melodramatic about the game. It's mostly a thriller/s-f so people who feel offended - shouldn't be.[/u]

[h3][b]RULES[/b][/h3]

[olist]
[*]The Challenge starts today and will last a year (this entry contains several elements that may suggest the correct answer). 
[*]Every 2 weeks there will be a devlog, in which elements of some movie will be hidden. 
[*]The name of the movie will be associated with one of 6 feelings.
[*]To each feeling, 3 movies are assigned. 
[*]Players have to guess which feeling we are talking about and what movie is being talked about. 
[*]There should be around 3 to 5 elements in each devlog that is related to a film.

[b]The time has come for our first Announcement![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/72c872c62ffee9b9843a6595c3e215342850534c.png[/img]

Taking advantage of today's [u]International Day of the Opposition to GMO's[/u] we would like to invite everyone for a discussion about Human Farm - we want to talk about matters of great importance as well as the more trivial ones called "[b]pleasant[/b]".


After revealing the Human Farm teaser trailer, we have noticed that it evoked extreme emotions. Many people who watched the presented trailer, found in it elements of vegan "propaganda", references to Orwell's work and such films as "Matrix", "Animal Farm", "1984", "They Live" and several others. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/3e6469d7f3ef7b0b9cedda577993450b9507ce55.png[/img]

At this time developers of the game do not want to reveal the whole intention of creating such a game. 

Only for this moment, we can say that some problems in the game will be presented literally, while others will be treated metaphorically, and still, others will be very ambiguous. Only the player, his interest, perceptiveness, and intelligence will determine whether he will find and understand them all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/5e33370e12aecec0c771f930fac11091a61bf74b.jpg[/img]

Without a doubt, the game will address very important matters and many elements of our present life. 


The whole story line up will be an important part of the game. 
With this in mind, however, we cannot forget that it will be a GAME,
and the games are mainly created for players. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/1774f88bfbce3964cb78a9aab1e3144de656767b.gif[/img]


We would like to know not only the opinions of people not related to the games but the players themselves. From the beginning, we planned to work closely with our fans. So we would like to ask you - the gamers -  what would you like to see in Human Farm? How do you think the game should look like, what do you want us to avoid and what must be included in the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37280190/558ee893f535e021367cda740eaa4d9159d01033.jpg[/img]

Every opinion matters to us, as the game is about the humankind itself.
